mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the following 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% and UNRATE declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS above their respective 12-month averages in the same month signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A co-movement between HOUST (new single-family houses sold) and GDPC1 (real GDP) where HOUST rises while GDPC1 falls in the same month indicates a divergence between housing demand and overall economic activity, which foreshadows a pullback in consumer confidence and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while GDPC1 decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such divergence months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL (Consumer Price Index) below 2% while FEDFUNDS remains above 2.5% for two consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive monetary policy, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% and FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for three consecutive quarters (annualized)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).
